adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 7.6. Thanksgiving (event week) has a historical median lift of x1.19 vs baseline, but noise-adjusted is x1.0—insufficient evidence to justify a lift. The price increase to $9.03 (+2.3%) is above prior price points; past price hikes (e.g., 2026-09-28, 2026-10-05) saw no sales lift, and the product is price-sensitive. Planner note: supplier delivery short—this introduces supply risk, lowering demand. No past promotion at this price or event. The classical uplift model suggests x1.0, which aligns with weak evidence. No drivers justify a move from baseline. Confidence is medium due to thin historical signal.

  events: Holiday: Thanksgiving (Thu)
  shelf price: 9.03 (+2.3% vs regular price 8.83)
  planner notes: Supplier warns of a short delivery

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 7.6 | 5%-95%: 0.0 - 40.1 | 10%-90%: 0.0 - 25.7

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-64% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
